content: 1. The natural history and autopsy findings of cryptococcal infections were detailed in a study published in the European Journal of Clinical Microbiology and Infectious Diseases in 2001. 2. A retrospective study conducted in Rwanda examined 37 cases of pulmonary cryptococcosis associated with HIV-1 infection, as reported in AIDS in 1994. 3. An epidemiological and diagnostic analysis of AIDS-associated cryptococcal meningitis in Rwanda from 1983 to 1992 was published in the Journal of Infection in 1999. 4. A study in São Paulo, Brazil, focused on detecting the capsular polysaccharide antigen of Cryptococcus neoformans in AIDS patients with neurocryptococcosis, as reported in the Revista do Instituto de Medicina Tropical de São Paulo in 1991. 5. Research in Australia and New Zealand explored the epidemiology and hostand variety-dependent characteristics of Cryptococcus neoformans infections, as published in Clinical Infectious Diseases in 2000. 6. The New England Journal of Medicine in 1989 discussed infections caused by Cryptococcus neoformans in patients with acquired immunodeficiency syndrome (AIDS). 7. A study in Kinshasa, Zaire, evaluated the utility of cryptococcal serum antigen screening among HIV-positive/AIDS patients, as reported in AIDS in 1989. 8. Cryptococcosis in HIV-infected children was analyzed in a study published in the Southeast Asian Journal of Tropical Medicine and Public Health in 2004. 9. A study compared the clinical presentation and monitoring of serum cryptococcal antigen titers in patients with and without HIV, as published in the Journal of Microbiology, Immunology, and Infection in 2009. 10. Population-based surveillance for cryptococcosis in an antiretroviral-naive South African province with high HIV seroprevalence was reported in AIDS in 2006. 11. A clinical epidemiological study of 171 cases of cryptococcosis was published in Clinical Infectious Diseases in 1994. 12. The detection of Cryptococcus using conventional, serological, and molecular methods was discussed in the Journal of Medical Microbiology in 2009. 13. A commercial enzyme immunoassay for detecting cryptococcal antigen was evaluated in a study published in Mycoses in 1993. 14. The diagnostic utility of the cryptococcal antigen test for AIDS-associated cryptococcosis in Rwanda was assessed in the Annales de la Société Belge de Médecine Tropicale in 1992. 15. A comparison of commercial kits for detecting cryptococcal antigen was published in the Journal of Clinical Microbiology in 1994. 16. The profile of central nervous system diseases in HIV/AIDS patients, with a focus on cryptococcal infections, was discussed in The Neurologist in 2008. 17. An enzyme immunoassay for detecting cryptococcal capsular polysaccharide antigen in serum and cerebrospinal fluid was evaluated in the Journal of Clinical Microbiology in 1993. 18. A study compared the PREMIER cryptococcal antigen enzyme immunoassay and the latex agglutination assay for detecting cryptococcal antigens, as published in the Journal of Clinical Microbiology in 1991. 19. A new enzyme immunoassay for detecting cryptococcal antigen was introduced in the Journal of Clinical Pathology in 1992. 20. A novel point-of-care lateral flow assay for detecting cryptococcal antigen in plasma and cerebrospinal fluid was evaluated at the 19th Conference on Retroviruses and Opportunistic Infections in 2012. 21. The IMMY cryptococcal antigen lateral flow assay was evaluated for detecting cryptococcal antigen at the Australian Society for Microbiology Annual Scientific Meeting in 2012. 22. The performance of a novel lateral-flow assay for detecting cryptococcal disease was presented at Infectious Disease Week in 2012. 23. A large-scale evaluation of immuno-mycologics lateral flow and enzyme-linked immunoassays for detecting cryptococcal antigen in serum and cerebrospinal fluid was published in Clinical Vaccine Immunology in 2013. 24. The CrAg LFA (cryptococcal antigen lateral flow assay) was described as a diagnostic tool, with details accessible online as of January 2018. 25. Findings from 4,961 suspected cases of adult meningitis in a setting with high HIV and TB prevalence were reported in BMC Infectious Diseases in 2010. 26. A case series on the clinical profile of disseminated cryptococcal infection was published in the Asian Pacific Journal of Tropical Medicine in 2010. 27. Cryptococcal infection in a cohort of HIV-1-infected Ugandan adults was analyzed in AIDS in 2002. 28. The value of serum cryptococcal antigen in diagnosing cryptococcal infection in HIV-infected patients was discussed in the Journal of Infection in 1990. 29. A novel point-of-care cryptococcal antigen test on serum, plasma, and urine from patients with HIV-associated cryptococcal meningitis was evaluated in Clinical Infectious Diseases in 2011. 30. The diagnostic accuracy of a fingerstick cryptococcal antigen lateral flow assay in HIV-infected persons was assessed in Clinical Infectious Diseases in 2015. 31. Cryptococcal antigen screening in patients initiating antiretroviral therapy in South Africa was studied in a prospective cohort, as published in Clinical Infectious Diseases in 2016. 32. A newly developed lateral flow immunoassay for diagnosing cryptococcosis was evaluated in Clinical Infectious Diseases in 2011. 33. Respiratory cryptococcosis in HIV-positive patients was discussed in the Revista Iberoamericana de Micología in 1999. 34. The failure of the cryptococcal serum antigen test to detect primary pulmonary cryptococcosis in HIV-infected patients was reported in Clinical Infectious Diseases in 1994. 35. Multisite validation of the cryptococcal antigen lateral flow assay and quantification by laser thermal contrast was published in Emerging Infectious Diseases in 2014. 36. A comparison of four assays for detecting cryptococcal antigen was published in Clinical Vaccine Immunology in 2012. 37. A multicenter evaluation of a novel point-of-care assay for detecting cryptococcal antigen in HIV-infected persons with and without cryptococcal meningitis was presented at the 52nd Interscience Conference on Antimicrobial Agents and Chemotherapy in 2012.
